README: OPERATING PROFILES for DJI Agras airframes. DATA, not code: adding a model
is an edit to this file.
THIS FILE IS NOT THE AIRCRAFT DIRECTORY. aircraftDirectory.json says which
airframes exist and what DJI publishes about them, and every figure there is
read off a manufacturer page or left null. This file is the layer above it:
the numbers a job estimate needs, which are mostly OPERATING RANGES rather
than published constants. Where the two disagree about tank capacity, the
directory and the operator win. See agrasProfiles.ts for the precedence.
WHY RANGES. Swath, flight height and speed are not properties of the
airframe, they are a working envelope. A T50 covering 11 m is a T50 flown
fast and high; the same aircraft on a slow in-canopy pass covers far less.
So each is stored as [min, max] and every default is the MIDPOINT, never the
maximum. A maximum is reachable in ideal conditions only, and defaulting to
it under-estimates every job in the same direction, which is the worst kind
of error: consistent, invisible, and always optimistic.
`source` is the provenance of those ranges. field-derived means operators and
extension trials, not a DJI page. `unverified` lists the fields nobody has
checked against a current spec sheet: those fields are null rather than
guessed, and any estimate that depends on one says so on screen.
IMPERIAL EQUIVALENTS ARE DERIVED, NEVER STORED. Gallons, feet and mph come
from lib/units.ts on the way to a screen. Two stored copies of one number is
two numbers that drift apart, and the one that drifts is always the one
somebody read.
See src/lib/agrasProfiles.ts for the schema and src/lib/jobEstimate.ts for
what consumes it.

profiles.note: 13 m of swath only appears at the top of the speed and height ranges. Field reports describe overheat warnings on low-speed high-rate passes, which is why the cooling constraint in the estimator matters most on this airframe.
Sprayers101 measured effective swath at no more than 7 m for in-canopy fungicide work on this class, against an advertised 11 m. The estimator caps in-canopy jobs there.
One published flow figure rather than a two-and-four-nozzle pair, so the two-nozzle entry is null.
Flow, battery and hover time have not been read off a current DJI page. Left null rather than carried over from the T40.
Hover time is quoted as 7 minutes loaded, without the takeoff weight it was measured at, so the weight stays null.

The directory carries a published 12 L/min for this airframe. It is not repeated here because nobody has confirmed which nozzle count it describes, and the estimator would present it as a rate ceiling.

Discontinued and the DJI specification page is gone. The 20 L here is the commonly quoted figure, which is why it is listed unverified: the directory refuses to state a capacity for this airframe at all, and a figure the operator reads off their own machine beats both.
Discontinued, page gone. See the T20 note: the capacity is quoted, not published, and the T10 carrying 8 L shows the model number does not encode it.
DJI publishes a nozzle-dependent 1.8 to 3 L/min for this airframe and the directory carries it. Not repeated here, for the same reason as the T20P.
No dry spreader for this airframe, so dry_spread_kg is null and that is a fact about the aircraft rather than a missing figure. Shares its operating envelope with the MG-1S.
Same envelope as the MG-1P. The two are one row in the source table and are split here so a fleet row resolves to the airframe it names.
